$comment: Phase 4 graph decision. Machine-readable companion to docs/GRAPH-DECISION.md. Every number here was measured on this machine on 2026-09-26 against the graph built 2026-09-19. If a number and the document disagree, the document is authoritative and this file is the bug.
not: a replacement for retrieval, and not a default

routing.consult_graph_when: retrieval's answer looks incomplete, not first

measured.reading: retrieval currently beats the graph on direct lookup and fusion is worse than either; the decision is a routing rule, not a ranking claim, because the graph is not competing to return the best single document

why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.finding: RETRACTED 2026-09-26: _FILE_CHAR_CAP does not truncate the corpus
why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.status: not a defect in the installed version (0.9.67)
why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.evidence: llm.py:2619-2621 pre-splits oversized documents into slices covering the whole file (upstream fix #1369); the code comment at llm.py:631-632 states the cap is a no-op for slices
why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.error_made: the first draft of this decision read a per-slice size limit as a whole-file size limit, inferred loss from file sizes, and never tested what the extractor actually receives
why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.effect_on_decision: none; the reason for keeping the graph was that 0.028 was a floor on a truncated corpus, and that premise is gone. The decision now rests on the association argument
why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.version_caveat: the graph was built by 0.9.46 and 0.9.67 is installed; whether 0.9.46 sliced .md (its set was {.md,.mdx,.markdown,.txt,.rst}) is unconfirmed, though this corpus is 100% .md so it should have

why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.finding: the graph holds structure retrieval cannot represent
why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.evidence: edge relations in the built graph
why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.implication: the conceptually_related_to layer is what the graph is for; the 0 wikilinks is an open item to check before the next rebuild

why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.finding: flat similarity cannot arbitrate claim identity, and scaling does not fix it

numbers.hard_negative_definition: anchor and negative share >=90% lexical similarity and differ only ontologically

why_keep_despite_scoring_lower.implication: this is why a symbolic layer is kept at all; a pure-vector stack cannot do this job at any model size

plan_claims_corrected.claim: markdown extraction is unreachable on the normal path; only watch.py reaches extract_markdown
plan_claims_corrected.verdict: no longer true in the installed version
plan_claims_corrected.evidence: extract.py:6678-6680 map .md/.mdx/.qmd to extract_markdown in the main dispatch table
plan_claims_corrected.corroboration: the built graph contains 2377 document nodes, which could not exist if markdown were skipped

plan_claims_corrected.claim: _FILE_CHAR_CAP truncates silently; a 229k-char file is read to 8.7%
plan_claims_corrected.verdict: wrong in this version; described a real historical bug, fixed upstream as #1369
plan_claims_corrected.evidence: installed 0.9.67 pre-splits oversized files into gap-free slices covering the whole file; verified 250/250 files reassemble byte-identically. The plan was written against older behaviour. I repeated this error in the first draft of this document, which is why the correction is recorded rather than quietly patched.

unresolved_on_purpose.question: LightRAG claims 67.6-84.8% win rates; the HippoRAG 2 aligned reproduction scores 16.6/2.4 direct and 1.6/11.6/2.4 multi-hop F1
unresolved_on_purpose.why_not_settled: both are third-party numbers on other people's datasets; nothing in this repository can adjudicate between them, and picking a side without running the comparison would assert a preference as a finding
unresolved_on_purpose.practical_consequence: do not adopt LightRAG on the strength of its own win-rate claim; if it is ever evaluated here, the reproduction's numbers are the prior

unresolved_on_purpose.question: whether 66.7% degrades to 39.06% under LLM-judge order/length/trial correction

upstream_defects.status: NOT a defect in 0.9.67; pre-slicing means no content is dropped

upstream_defects.location: no GRAPHIFY_* override, no config loader

upstream_defects.status: the real limitation for a relational graph
upstream_defects.impact: 991 of 1014 oversized files have slices split across >1 chunk; a prompt never contains two chunks, so conceptually_related_to cannot be emitted between them
upstream_defects.fix: raise --token-budget, or use --mode deep for INFERRED edges

upstream_defects.impact: the vault's own link structure may not be indexed as such

deployment_finding_keep_both_gradings.$comment: kept verbatim in every form because a reader who sees only one grading draws the wrong conclusion in one direction or the other
deployment_finding_keep_both_gradings.evidence: six independent papers report trials on the mechanism; the locally-deployed instance prints a complete plausible config with ENABLED = true and TOP_PERCENT_SURPRISAL = 0.1, and the same file records the dream cycle as 404 and surprisal as disabled

do_not_claim: that 13-22 hours is an upstream ingestion figure; it is the owner's own measured run, found in no graphify doc, issue, or PR
that ingestion is free and local; markdown is 100% the expensive LLM pass, while the free deterministic tree-sitter AST pass is for code

code_that_encodes_this.behaviour: the associative graph is a second candidate source, never a default; it fires on the deliberative route or on a turn with enough distinct concepts that one document is unlikely to hold the whole answer

review_triggers: a rebuild at a higher --token-budget, or with --mode deep; the 0.028 was measured at the 60k default where 991 of 1014 large files span more than one chunk
the corpus grows substantially; multi-hop needs enough documents for a path to exist
a wikilink relation appears in the built graph, or its absence is explained
the slicer's behaviour is confirmed against 0.9.46, the version that built the current graph
